findings.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Hits @antv Ecosystem, 639 Compromised npm Package Versions
findings.summary_md: Socket's original disclosure of the May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud wave that this September GitHub Actions re-infection descends from. 639 compromised npm versions across 323 unique packages were tied to the atool maintainer account, concentrated in @antv packages and echarts-for-react with roughly 1.1 million weekly downloads. The payload exfiltrates RSA+AES encrypted data to t.m-kosche[.]com disguised as OpenTelemetry traces and also commits stolen secrets to public GitHub repositories with Dune-themed names and the reversed marker "Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again". Across the full campaign Socket tracked 1,055 compromised versions across 502 packages spanning npm, PyPI, and Composer, and counted roughly 1.9k attacker exfiltration repositories.

findings.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Strikes Again: 317 npm Packages Compromised
findings.summary_md: SafeDep's May 19, 2026 analysis of the same campaign: 637 malicious versions were published across 317 packages in a 22-minute automated burst, hitting packages with 15M+ combined monthly downloads including size-sensor, echarts-for-react, and timeago.js. The 498KB obfuscated Bun payload harvests CI and developer credentials, injects Claude Code SessionStart hooks and VS Code folderOpen tasks, installs the kitty-monitor dead-drop C2 backdoor that polls GitHub commit search for RSA-PSS signed commands containing the keyword firedalazer, and exfiltrates through the GitHub Git Data API and t.m-kosche[.]com. This is the payload analysis the September re-infection reporting points back to, including the wiper, the gh-token-monitor polling daemon, and the Dune-named exfiltration repository pattern.
